name: Tesamorelin
summary: An FDA-approved, lab-made version of the brain hormone that triggers growth hormone release, used to shrink excess deep belly fat in adults with HIV.
what_it_is: Tesamorelin is a synthetic version of growth hormone-releasing factor (GRF): the full 44-amino-acid hormone with a small chemical group (hexenoyl) attached. It signals the pituitary gland to release the body's own growth hormone, which raises IGF-1 and reduces deep abdominal (visceral) fat. It is sold as Egrifta SV and Egrifta WR and has been FDA-approved since 2010.

evidence.why: Two randomized, placebo-controlled trials in 816 adults with HIV supported its approval for reducing visceral fat; other uses (fatty liver, thinking skills) rest on single smaller trials.

status_us.label: FDA-approved (Egrifta) for HIV-related belly fat
status_us.note: Approved since 2010 to reduce excess abdominal fat in adults with HIV who have lipodystrophy; the label says it is not a weight-loss drug and its long-term heart safety is not established. WADA bans it in sport.

benefits.claim: Cut visceral (deep belly) fat by roughly 15% over 26 weeks versus placebo in adults with HIV and excess abdominal fat; the fat came back in people who stopped
Lowered triglycerides and improved the cholesterol ratio in adults with HIV and excess abdominal fat
Reduced liver fat over 12 months in 61 adults with HIV and fatty liver disease
Improved executive function (planning and attention) over 20 weeks in 152 older adults with or without mild cognitive impairment

risks.risk: Injection-site reactions such as redness, itching or pain (17% vs 6% on placebo)
Fluid-retention effects: joint pain, swelling of the limbs, tingling or numbness, and occasionally carpal tunnel syndrome
Very high IGF-1: about a third had IGF-1 more than 3 standard deviations above normal at 26 weeks; long-term effects unknown
Higher blood sugar: 5% vs 1% reached a diabetes-range HbA1c at 26 weeks
Allergic reactions such as itching, flushing, hives or rash (4% in trials)

More deaths have been reported with growth hormone-type drugs during acute critical illness (after heart or abdominal surgery, major trauma, or acute respiratory failure); the label says to consider stopping it in critically ill patients

avoid_if: Damage to the hypothalamic-pituitary axis (pituitary tumor or surgery, head radiation, major head trauma)
Known allergy to tesamorelin or its ingredients
interactions: Glucocorticoid replacement for adrenal insufficiency: higher maintenance or stress doses may be needed
Drugs cleared by liver CYP450 enzymes (e.g., corticosteroids, sex steroids, anticonvulsants, cyclosporine): the label advises monitoring when combined

during: IGF-1 (the label suggests considering stopping for persistent large elevations)
Eye exams for retinopathy in people with diabetes
labs.why: The label calls for checking blood sugar before and during treatment and monitoring IGF-1, because tesamorelin raises IGF-1 and can cause glucose intolerance.

studies.title: Metabolic Effects of a Growth Hormone-Releasing Factor in Patients with HIV
studies.people: 412 adults with HIV and excess abdominal fat
studies.finding: Over 26 weeks, visceral fat fell 15.2% with tesamorelin and rose 5.0% with placebo, and triglycerides and cholesterol ratios improved, with no significant change in fasting glucose. About half of treated patients developed antibodies to the drug.

studies.title: Effects of tesamorelin on non-alcoholic fatty liver disease in HIV: a randomised, double-blind, multicentre trial
studies.people: 61 adults with HIV and fatty liver
studies.finding: Over 12 months, liver fat fell 37% from baseline relative to placebo, and 35% vs 4% reached normal liver fat; blood sugar did not differ between groups.

studies.title: Effects of growth hormone-releasing hormone on cognitive function in adults with mild cognitive impairment and healthy older adults: results of a controlled trial
studies.people: 152 adults aged 55 to 87, 66 with mild cognitive impairment
studies.finding: After 20 weeks, tesamorelin improved executive function versus placebo in both groups and reduced body fat by 7.4%. Mild side effects were more common than on placebo (68% vs 36%).

studies.title: EGRIFTA WR (tesamorelin) for injection: prescribing information (revised March 2025)
studies.people: 816 adults with HIV in two 26-week randomized trials, plus extensions
studies.finding: Visceral fat fell 14-18% versus little change on placebo; people switched to placebo for another 26 weeks regained it.

ask_your_clinician: Has a scan or waist measurement confirmed excess visceral fat, and what result would show it is working?
How will we track my blood sugar and IGF-1, and at what point would we stop?
What happens to the fat I lose if I stop treatment?

notes_for_editor: Seed claims checked against the March 2025 label: contraindications, IGF-1/glucose monitoring and loss of effect after stopping are confirmed. The label also warns of increased mortality in acute critical illness after open-heart surgery (consider stopping in critically ill patients), left out above for space. The cognition trial abstract was read on QxMD because PubMed/PMC pages were blocked by a browser check. The label gives no DEA schedule. EU and Canada status were not rechecked.
